title: Portfolio CMS
longDescription:
Overview

Portfolio CMS is a bespoke Content Management System (CMS) designed to bridge the gap between static site generation and dynamic content management. Built to run entirely within the Google Workspace ecosystem, it transforms a simple Google Sheet into a powerful database and backend for a professional, React-based portfolio website. This project eliminates the need for traditional hosting fees, complex database setups, or third-party CMS subscriptions, offering a truly serverless and zero-cost solution for creatives.

Key Features

  • Spreadsheet-as-a-Database: Utilizes Google Sheets as a relational database to store project metadata, categorized tags, gallery links, and global site settings.
  • Visual Admin Interface: A custom-built, responsive web application (deployed via Google Apps Script) serves as the admin panel. It features:
  • Rich Text Editing: Integrated Quill.js editors for formatting project descriptions with bold, italics, lists, and headers.
  • Dynamic List Management: Drag-and-drop style interfaces for managing gallery images and downloadable files.
  • Live Preview & Publishing: One-click publishing that generates a static HTML file, injects the latest data, and saves it directly to Google Drive for hosting via GitHub Pages or similar platforms.
  • Smart Automation:
  • Featured Project Logic: Automatically handles "Featured" status across categories, ensuring only one project per category is highlighted on the hero board.
  • Media Handling: Automatically detects YouTube links to generate thumbnails and embedded players, while standardizing image URLs.
  • Data Sanitization: Cleans and formats incoming data to ensure consistent front-end rendering.
  • Modern Front-End: The generated website is a single-file React application styled with Tailwind CSS, featuring:
  • Glassmorphism Design: A modern, dark-mode aesthetic with blurred backdrops and smooth transitions.
  • Responsive Layouts: Fully adaptive grids for mobile, tablet, and desktop views.
  • Interactive Components: Custom-built lightboxes, modals, and navigation menus.

Technical Stack

  • Backend: Google Apps Script (Serverless Node.js environment)
  • Database: Google Sheets API
  • Frontend (Admin): HTML5, Tailwind CSS, Vanilla JavaScript
  • Frontend (Public Site): React 18, Tailwind CSS, Lucide React Icons
  • Integrations: EmailJS (Serverless contact form), Google Analytics 4

The "Why"

As a multidisciplinary designer, I needed a way to update my portfolio without touching code every time I finished a project. Existing solutions were either too rigid (Wix/Squarespace) or too complex/expensive for a simple static site (Contentful/Sanity). Portfolio CMS was born from the desire to own the entire stack—data, logic, and presentation—while keeping the maintenance overhead near zero.

title: Main Room - Temple Nightclub | San Francisco
description: A comprehensive, hybrid lighting and video installation engineered for seamless cross-system pixel mapping and total venue immersion.
longDescription:
The main room remodel at Temple Nightclub in San Francisco is a dense, hybrid lighting and video installation designed to deliver maximum environmental immersion and operational flexibility. The core architecture integrates a curved video ceiling that wraps behind the DJ, ten custom floor-to-ceiling LED pixel pillars, and a vast array of moving wash fixtures. The primary differentiator of this design is its meticulous flat-black construction across all hardware components. This design choice allows the entire complex infrastructure to vanish completely into the dark when unlit, contrasting sharply with the massive visual output of the active rig.


Constructed during the 2020 pandemic shutdown, the installation required profound physical and electrical infrastructure modifications before aesthetic integration could begin. To safely accommodate the curved video ceiling, a fire-suppression team was brought in to entirely reroute the sprinklers to deploy beneath the wall. The venue's power capacity was completely overhauled with new 400-amp and 200-amp services and breaker panels, feeding a meticulously mapped network of dedicated and shared circuits based on strict component specifications. Operational efficiency was prioritized throughout the physical build; all rig power was placed on switched relays for centralized shut-down, and independent, hardwired house lighting was installed to allow staff maintenance without activating the complex show systems.


The defining technical achievement of the installation is the cohesive, cross-system pixel mapping infrastructure layered on top of this robust electrical foundation. By linking the video playback engine directly to the room's environmental lighting—including custom edge-lit VIP tables, illuminated booths, and a double-sided dancefloor monolith—the system translates localized video content into precise color and intensity data distributed across the entire venue. To manage the sheer density and potential output of this rig, the operational strategy enforces highly selective, limited use across all combined systems. This strict design discipline avoids over-lighting the dancefloor while ensuring massive, unified full-room looks can be generated efficiently from centralized media inputs.


Specs

(144) PixelDots

(12) 150w Hybrid Zoom Lights

(40) RGBWA+UV Wash Fixtures

(2) Radiance Hazers

(6400) RGBW LED Pixel Pillars

(234) 1m x 0.5m Video Panels (4.81p)

(60) 0.5m x 0.5m Video Panels (4.81p)

title: LithoLab
description: A fully browser-based web application for generating custom-shaped, multi-color 3D printable lithophanes with AI-assisted design tools.
longDescription:
LithoLab is a client-side web application designed to generate high-fidelity, custom-shaped lithophanes for 3D printing. While standard generators are restricted to traditional four-color CMYK constraints, LithoLab supports customizable, multi-color palettes to achieve superior color accuracy in the final physical print. The project differentiates itself by introducing custom masking capabilities that trim the lithophane into non-standard shapes, along with generating an independently exportable geometric border for polished, multi-part assemblies.


The system architecture was developed by porting the open-source PIXEStl backend to execute entirely within the browser, avoiding server-side processing overhead. The workflow is managed through a custom frontend interface where users upload source imagery, define masking parameters, and configure border dimensions. Upon export, the software isolates the customized border as a discrete 3D object, allowing users to assign specific filaments and colors when preparing the files in slicing software like Bambu Studio.


The standout technical achievement is the robust JavaScript implementation of the modified PIXEStl engine, paired with an integrated Google Gemini API for generating base images, structural masks, and file metadata. To solve the hardware constraints of color mapping on advanced machines like the Bambu Lab X1C, a dedicated companion utility called LithoPalletGen was built in parallel. This secondary application handles precise color palette generation, import/export functionality, and material calibration to ensure accurate physical reproduction of the digital models.

title: Unfold
description: Unfold is a high-fidelity reflection platform that transforms prompt-based journaling into an interactive, digital experience. Unlike static journaling applications, Unfold utilizes a dynamic card-shuffling engine and a sophisticated deck-based architecture to provide structured introspection. Its primary value lies in its ability to balance pre-curated psychological prompts with a robust user-defined content system, making it adaptable for both therapeutic use and creative professional workflows.
longDescription:
Unfold is a high-fidelity reflection platform that transforms prompt-based journaling into an interactive, digital experience. Unlike static journaling applications, Unfold utilizes a dynamic card-shuffling engine and a sophisticated deck-based architecture to provide structured introspection. Its primary value lies in its ability to balance pre-curated psychological prompts with a robust user-defined content system, making it adaptable for both therapeutic use and creative professional workflows.


The application is organized into three functional modules: the Journey Setup for session parameterization, the immersive Card Display for active reflection, and a History Panel for auditing past insights. Users navigate from an initial configuration phase through a focused session where they can flip cards, mark favorites, and track their progress through a deck. This workflow ensures that data moves seamlessly from high-level session parameters to granular, individual prompt interactions and eventual long-term archival.


Built on a modern React and TypeScript foundation, Unfold prioritizes performance and data privacy. The technical core features a custom-built state management layer using React Hooks and the LocalStorage API, ensuring all sensitive user reflections remain strictly client-side. The UI is powered by Tailwind CSS and Radix UI primitives, providing an accessible, responsive, and aesthetically refined interface that maintains smooth transitions during complex deck interactions.

title: Pixel Pyramid
description: A 3D-printed, single-print LED pixel art sculpture utilizing clear shells and software-limited thermal management for maximum brightness.
longDescription:
The LED pixel pyramid is an internally divided, single-print pixel art sculpture. The primary goal was to create a vibrant, multi-material light installation without the need for complex post-print assembly. While early proofs of concept were successfully prototyped on an IDEX printer using standard black and white filaments, the opaque outer shell severely limited the light transmission to dark environments. By shifting to a clear top shell, the design maximizes luminosity and creates a much more versatile display piece.


The fabrication process relies heavily on the speed and multi-material capabilities of the Bambu Lab X1C. Moving from rough prototypes to the final model requires continuous printing over a 1 to 3-day cycle, with three filament swaps occurring on every layer. While this approach achieves the necessary visual quality and structural integrity, it introduces unique challenges with material swap waste, which will inform future optimizations using tool-changer machines.


The primary engineering hurdle involved managing the trapped internal heat generated by the LEDs, which threatened to warp the 3D-printed structure over time. To solve this, precision software-side current limiting was implemented via WLED. This ensures a perfect balance between maximum visual brightness and safe thermal dynamics, preserving the integrity of the piece.


Specs

Medium: PLA+ (3 material)

Color: Black, White, Transparent

LEDs: 256

Driver: WS2815 (RGB)

Decoder: ATHOM (ESP8266)

Software: WLED

title: LVL - Temple | Denver
description: An electrical and data overhaul of an immersive pixel lighting rig to ensure stability and enable 3D voxel mapping.
longDescription:
The LVL room at Temple Denver features an immersive, exclusively pixel-based lighting installation with continuous lines running across the floor, ceiling, and pillars. The core goal of this project was to execute a comprehensive structural rewiring of the power and data distribution to transform an unstable installation into a robust, production-ready system. Unlike standard rig assemblies, this overhaul required retrofitting an existing design, demanding precise power management and signal integrity to support advanced, whole-room spatial mapping without compromising the original aesthetic.


The project workflow centered on meticulous hardware restoration and systemic reconfiguration. Every segment of the existing LED tape was systematically removed, rigorously tested, resoldered, heat-shrinked, and reinstalled to guarantee structural and electrical integrity. To handle the data load, the LED decoder lines were strategically decentralized across the network. Concurrently, the entire power infrastructure was redesigned, efficiently routing power from supplies located in the back room and beneath the DJ booth to ensure consistent performance across the venue's footprint.


The primary technical constraint of the installation was the extreme length of the pixel runs, which inherently caused severe voltage drop and data signal degradation. This was overcome by running DC wire in parallel with the LED strips to introduce strategic power injection points, guaranteeing uniform brightness and absolute data stability. With the hardware stabilized, the entire room was 3D voxel mapped, allowing the control system to execute volumetric, full-room effects like spatial line sweeps. By isolating specific structural elements into distinct groups, the system can also effectively simulate the behavior of traditional lighting fixtures within a continuous pixel environment.

title: Pixel Inflatable Tubes - Reelworks | Denver
description: Custom ultra-bright LED illumination architecture designed for 100-foot inflatable centerpieces at Denver Pride 2023.
longDescription:
This project delivered the centerpiece lighting architecture for Reelworks and Tracks during Denver Pride 2023, designed specifically to illuminate massive 100-foot inflatable tubes. The primary objective was to achieve an exceptionally high brightness level capable of standing out in a highly saturated live event environment. To exceed standard luminous constraints, the project bypassed off-the-shelf solutions in favor of custom-manufactured pixel strands. These bespoke strands featured double-sided LEDs housed behind clear lenses, maximizing light transmission and ensuring high-fidelity color rendering from every viewing angle.


Executing the design required a precise electrical and mechanical workflow to manage extreme cable lengths and power demands. Two of the custom 100-foot LED strands were run in parallel inside each inflatable structure to compound the overall brightness. Overcoming the inevitable voltage drop across a 100-foot span required an isolated power distribution strategy. Power supplies were strategically mounted at both ends of the tubes, and the positive voltage lines were physically severed at the midpoint. This safely prevented power back-feeding between the discrete power supply units while allowing data to travel seamlessly across the entire fixture.


The technical foundation of the installation was built on a 24V LED system equipped with redundant data lines, mitigating the risk of pixel failure during the live show. Visual programming and real-time system control were driven entirely through Resolume Arena for large-scale pixel mapping. A significant engineering constraint emerged regarding signal transmission: while wireless decoders performed flawlessly during closed testing, the deployment revealed severe RF interference caused by the dense concentration of attendee cell phones. This provided a critical validation for utilizing hardwired data infrastructure to maintain system stability in electromagnetically noisy, large-scale event spaces.

title: GeoLens Pro
description: GeoLens Pro is a mobile-first Progressive Web Application (PWA) designed for field professionals who need to capture, organize, and annotate geo-tagged photos. The app solves the common problem of managing large volumes of field photos by automatically sorting them based on GPS location into predefined job zones.
longDescription:
GeoLens Pro - Portfolio Breakdown

Overview

GeoLens Pro is a mobile-first Progressive Web Application (PWA) designed for field professionals who need to capture, organize, and annotate geo-tagged photos. The app solves the common problem of managing large volumes of field photos by automatically sorting them based on GPS location into predefined job zones.


The Problem It Solves

Field workers (surveyors, inspectors, contractors, real estate professionals) often capture hundreds of photos across multiple job sites. Manually organizing these photos is:

  • Time-consuming - Hours spent sorting and renaming files
  • Error-prone - Photos easily get assigned to wrong projects
  • Disconnected - No link between photos, locations, and client data


The Solution

GeoLens Pro uses GPS geofencing to automatically sort photos into jobs the moment they're captured. If you're standing at a job site and take a photo, the app knows exactly which job it belongs to - no manual sorting required.


Core Features

1. GPS-Powered Auto-Sort Engine

The heart of the application. When a photo is captured or imported:

  1. GPS coordinates are extracted (live from device or from EXIF metadata)
  2. The Haversine formula calculates the distance to each active job's origin
  3. If the photo falls within a job's geofence radius, it's automatically assigned
  4. If multiple jobs overlap, the closest one wins
  5. Photos outside all zones go to "Unassigned" for manual sorting
// Haversine formula implementation for GPS distance
const R = 6371000; // Earth's radius in meters
const distance = R * c; // Distance between photo and job origin
if (distance <= job.radius) → Assign to job


2. Job Management with Geofencing

  • Define job locations using an interactive Leaflet map
  • Set custom geofence radii (feet, meters, miles, or kilometers)
  • Visual radius preview on the map
  • Jobs can be Active or Archived
  • Smart sorting options: Recent Activity, A-Z, Newest, Oldest


3. Client CRM

  • Full contact management (company, contact person, email, phone, address)
  • Link clients to jobs for organized project tracking
  • Alphabetically sorted client list
  • Swipe-to-delete with confirmation


4. Camera Integration

  • Live camera mode with real-time GPS indicator
  • Front/rear camera toggle
  • Flash control
  • Photo import with EXIF metadata extraction
  • High-resolution capture (up to 4032x3024)


5. Advanced Photo Editor

  • Multi-layer transparency system - Create annotation layers like slides
  • Drawing tools - Brush and eraser with customizable colors and sizes
  • Image transforms - Rotate (90 degree increments), flip horizontal/vertical
  • Cropping - With coordinate system that maintains drawing positions
  • Per-layer transforms - Each layer can have its own crop/rotation
  • Undo/redo history
  • Layer management (add, delete, rename, reorder)


6. Slideshow Viewer

  • Fullscreen presentation mode
  • Swipe/tap navigation through all layers
  • Title and caption display
  • Navigation indicators


7. PDF Export

  • Professional document generation with jsPDF
  • Header with job title, client info, and location
  • 2x2 grid layout of all layers (Original + annotations)
  • Captions preserved under each image
  • Perfect for reports, documentation, or printing

title: PixelForge AI
description: PixelForge AI is a serverless, client-side generative art studio that leverages Google's Gemini and Imagen models. It features a robust local database for gallery management, intelligent prompt augmentation, and a "Bring Your Own Key" architecture that prioritizes user privacy and ease of deployment.
longDescription:
PixelForge AI is a dedicated workspace application designed to streamline the generation and curation of AI artwork. Unlike standard chat interfaces, this application provides a highly structured environment optimized specifically for image synthesis, exposing advanced granular controls like aspect ratios, negative prompts, and resolution settings. Its primary differentiator is the direct, flexible integration with Google's Imagen 4.0 API, supporting dual-endpoint routing to handle various generation parameters and safety filters natively.


The user journey is centered around a unified workspace module where creators construct and refine prompts using integrated templating tools. Once a generation is triggered, the asynchronous process is managed via global state, allowing users to continue working without interruption. Completed images flow directly into a comprehensive history dashboard, where users can inspect generation metadata, view high-resolution details, and export their assets in batch using built-in client-side ZIP compression capabilities.


Under the hood, the application is powered by a React 18 frontend written in TypeScript and styled with Tailwind CSS for a responsive, dark-mode-first aesthetic. Complex asynchronous API interactions and cross-component data synchronization are orchestrated seamlessly through Zustand, ensuring a highly performant and stable user experience even when handling large base64 image payloads.

title: Chronicle: Iterative Fiction Engine
description: Chronicle is a multi-modal interactive fiction engine designed to generate dynamic, choice-driven narratives in real time. Unlike traditional text adventures with pre-written paths, this application leverages generative AI to dynamically construct the story, illustrations, and voice narration based on continuous user decisions. Operating completely without a backend server, it securely orchestrates complex, multi-step API workflows directly from the client browser.
longDescription:
Chronicle is a multi-modal interactive fiction engine designed to generate dynamic, choice-driven narratives in real time. Unlike traditional text adventures with pre-written paths, this application leverages generative AI to dynamically construct the story, illustrations, and voice narration based on continuous user decisions. Operating completely without a backend server, it securely orchestrates complex, multi-step API workflows directly from the client browser.


The journey begins in a configuration interface where players define their desired genre, visual style, and initial premise. The application then transitions into a primary story terminal displaying narrative text, synthesized scene imagery, and audio playback controls. Throughout the experience, the system silently extracts lore to populate a living codex of entities and artifacts, while a built-in state manager allows users to pause, resume, or export their completed adventure as a formatted document.


Under the hood, the application is powered by a zero-infrastructure React architecture running within a single HTML file. It integrates the Google Gemini API for complex narrative generation and text-to-speech, paired with the Google Imagen API for stylized image synthesis, demonstrating advanced prompt engineering, resilient fallback handling, and robust client-side data persistence.

title: Strata - Digital Notebook
description: A modern, block-based note-taking web application with Google Drive integration and an infinite canvas workspace.
longDescription:
Overview

Strata is a full-featured note-taking app built with React, offering hierarchical organization, cloud sync, and a flexible canvas for visual notes. It runs entirely in the browser with no backend server, using Google Drive for cloud storage and localStorage as an offline fallback.


Key Features

Organizational Structure

  • Hierarchical organization: Notebooks → Tabs → Pages
  • Color-coded tabs with automatic cycling
  • Favorites system for quick access
  • Responsive tab navigation with fish-eye hover effects


Rich Text Editing

  • Block-based editor supporting headings, lists, todos, images, videos, links, and dividers
  • Slash commands (/) for quick block insertion
  • Drag-and-drop block reordering
  • Real-time formatting with keyboard shortcuts


Canvas Pages

  • Infinite canvas with pan and zoom (Alt+scroll wheel)
  • Freeform drawing with customizable brush colors and widths
  • Text containers for annotations
  • Image pasting and manipulation
  • Transform state persistence per page
  • Live drawing feedback


Cloud Integration

  • Google Drive sync with automatic debounced saves
  • Embed Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides directly in pages
  • PDF viewing from URLs or Google Drive
  • Portable backup system with offline viewer
  • Two-way sync with conflict resolution


User Experience

  • Full dark mode support
  • System preference detection for theme
  • Session-wide page caching for fast navigation
  • Offline support with localStorage fallback
  • No backend required — runs entirely client-side


Technical Highlights

  • Built with React (JSX) and transpiled in-browser with Babel
  • Google Drive API integration for cloud storage
  • Coordinate system handling for infinite canvas with viewport culling
  • Real-time drawing with SVG path rendering
  • Responsive design with Tailwind CSS
  • Zero-dependency architecture (except Google APIs)

title: IdeaForge.AI
description: IdeaForge AI is an ideation and execution workspace designed to eliminate the friction between conceptualizing a product and building it. It replaces fragmented note-taking tools by providing a continuous pipeline for raw idea capture, interactive brainstorming, and campaign management.
longDescription:
IdeaForge AI is a personal, AI-powered workspace designed to capture and structure raw creative thoughts. Unlike standard note-taking tools that rely on proprietary cloud backends, this application ensures total data sovereignty by utilizing the user's personal Google Drive and Google Sheets as a headless, relational database.


The application guides users through a structured creative lifecycle. The journey begins in the Ideas module, where users capture stream-of-consciousness text or voice notes. These raw inputs are processed by AI into organized concepts, which can then be escalated through dedicated Brainstorming workspaces, structured Project task boards, and final marketing Campaign trackers. 


Under the hood, the system is built on a modern React and TypeScript frontend, heavily utilizing TanStack Query for state management and data synchronization. Its primary technical achievement is the complex integration of the Google Sheets REST API to perform robust database operations—including filtering, row migrations, and schema updates—entirely client-side.

title: CharGen.AI
description: CharGen AI is a comprehensive design suite that automates the creation of multi-dimensional character profiles and visual assets. Unlike standard random generators, this application enforces strict logical consistency across psychological, physical, and demographic traits. It utilizes structured JSON generation via Google's Gemini API to ensure every attribute contextually aligns with the character's core identity.
longDescription:
CharGen AI is a comprehensive design suite that automates the creation of multi-dimensional character profiles and visual assets. Unlike standard random generators, this application enforces strict logical consistency across psychological, physical, and demographic traits. It utilizes structured JSON generation via Google's Gemini API to ensure every attribute contextually aligns with the character's core identity.


The application features a modular workflow guiding users from initial ideation to asset export. Users begin in the trait manipulation forms to fine-tune attributes like MBTI, physical build, and origin. This data feeds into the Generation Panel, where prompt engines synthesize visual representations—ranging from profile portraits to technical T-pose reference sheets—and author narrative backstories tailored to specific genres.


Built on a React and Vite frontend, the application utilizes Zustand for complex state management across its creation modules. The primary technical achievement is the custom prompt translation layer, which dynamically parses dozens of UI inputs into optimized, high-fidelity instructions for seamless integration with multimodal AI endpoints.

title: LithoPalletGen
description: A vanilla JavaScript color calibration tool utilizing area-averaged pixel sampling for precise multi-material lithophane generation.
longDescription:
LithoPalletGen is a specialized color calibration application designed to streamline multi-material lithophane workflows by accurately mapping printed filament swatches. Unlike standard single-pixel color pickers, this tool utilizes a configurable area-averaging eyedropper that samples regions ranging from 32 to 256 pixels. This distinct approach neutralizes surface noise, lighting variances, and filament translucency, ensuring statistically accurate color profiles that reflect the physical characteristics of the printed material.


The tool operates through a split-pane interface that directly pairs a canvas-based image viewer with a hierarchical palette builder. Users upload photographs of physical prints and systematically construct multi-layer color profiles, categorizing base colors alongside ordered layers of increasing material thickness. As users sample the image, a live-updating bounding box overlays the canvas, aggregating color data across hundreds of pixels to actively filter out the textural inconsistencies inherent in FDM prints.


Engineered as a zero-dependency vanilla JavaScript application with no build step, the system operates entirely client-side, utilizing IndexedDB for persistent image storage and localStorage for palette serialization. The core technical achievement is the real-time pixel averaging engine, which rapidly executes per-frame getImageData computations across large pixel arrays while maintaining fluid cursor responsiveness. A unified color model anchors the architecture, driving a dual-format export system that outputs PIXEstl-compatible JSON in either HSL or hex notation for immediate downstream processing.

title: Lobby Wall - Tracks | Denver
description: A modular, double-sided LED pixel wall engineered for rapid nightclub deployment and controlled via Madrix software.
longDescription:
This project involved designing and deploying a double-sided LED pixel wall for a major facility remodel at Tracks nightclub in Denver. To overcome a highly compressed installation window, the system was engineered as a fully modular framework rather than a traditional in-place build. This approach allowed for comprehensive off-site assembly and testing, minimizing on-site risk and enabling a complete installation over the course of just two days.


The fabrication process required custom physical formatting to achieve the necessary visual density. Raw LED pucks were manually soldered with custom wire lengths to account for specific pixel spacing requirements. These custom arrays were then contact-cemented onto standardized pegboard panels in eight-pixel configurations. This modular panelized workflow enabled rigorous pre-installation testing of every segment. Once mounted in the venue, the arrays were finished with frosted plexiglass panels secured on standoffs, providing even light diffusion across both sides of the wall.


The installation's hardware architecture relies on the WS2801 two-wire protocol, driven by a 16-output SanDevices E682 decoder. To streamline the physical wiring and digital mapping, the power and data topology was organized so that each horizontal row of pegboard modules connects to a dedicated output on the controller. The entire double-sided array is mapped and dynamically driven using Madrix 3.6 lighting control software, allowing for complex, real-time pixel manipulation across the network.


Specs

Fixtures: LED Pixels

Pixels: 520

Driver: WS2801 (RGB)

Decoder: SanDevices E682

Software: Madrix 3.6

title: Curved Bottle Shelf - Que Bueno Suerte! | Denver
image: media/Lighting/Curved Bottle Shelf - Que Bueno Suerte! _ Denver/Screenshot 2026-07-20 171107.webp
description: A custom-integrated, 3D-printed addressable LED lighting system designed to illuminate a central curved bottle shelf.
longDescription:
The objective of this project was to provide functional, elegant illumination for a custom-fabricated metal curved bottle shelf serving as the primary visual focal point at Que Bueno Suerte!. Instead of relying on standard off-the-shelf LED extrusions that often produce unwanted glare, the solution required a highly tailored approach. The core differentiator is a series of custom-designed, 3D-printed corner pixel fixtures featuring integrated louvers, specifically engineered to direct light toward the display while completely blocking direct sightlines to the diodes for passing guests.


The workflow centered on designing fixtures that matched the specific geometry of the existing metalwork. Following the fabrication phase, the physical installation prioritized seamless integration and discreet cable management to maintain a clean aesthetic. The entire pixel array was meticulously hardwired and routed using black wire wrap to blend directly into the shelf's architecture. This routing ensured the design of the metalwork remained uninterrupted by the underlying electrical infrastructure.


The technical execution relies on precisely manufactured physical components produced on Bambu Lab 3D printers, ensuring exact tolerances for the light-blocking louvers. Operationally, the individual fixtures function as part of a comprehensive, venue-wide network. The shelf's lighting system is fully tied into the restaurant's overarching control infrastructure and driven by a centralized server running Madrix 5.x, enabling robust, synchronized control over the installation.
